title: Wages and cheap suits in the 1930s
summary: Roy made thirty-two dollars at the Savoy and bought cheap suits, noting how far money went.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: What always amazes me about those days is that you were able to live. You just mentioned before the band would make eight dollars a week or something like that.
I guess you do whatever you can manage on that.

Well, I made thirty-two dollars in the Savoy, and every two weeks I bought me a suit. It wasn't a hundred-dollar suit. There was a cat that... Woolworth's was the place then. Woolworth's was the thing. I bought all them suits, and all of them went out of style. The suits all had buttons on the vest, and all these buttons... Heh-heh. And all of a sudden, the lounge came in, and here I am stuck with all these...heh-heh...

Now, money went a little farther than, you know. You could take ten dollars and go out and have a good time. You can't take ten dollars and do nothing now. You go in Ryan's and have two drinks, you're dead!
